Header: Veridian Cloud <> Redwood Inference - partner intro / discovery
Date/Time: 2026-11-18 15:30 UTC | Duration: ~54 minutes
Location: Zoom call (recording enabled)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Veridian Head of Partnerships), Jordan Lee (Veridian CTO), Alex Kim (Veridian Infra)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Quick partner intro. Veridian is a regional cloud provider focused on enterprise customers in APAC/EU with custom GPU racks and a federated control plane. Exploring integration options: marketplace listing, dedicated GPU pools, and a co-developed benchmark for Redwood model serving. Key asks: pricing, integration effort, security/compliance (SOC2, KMS), routing and latency guarantees. Next steps: deck + pricing, SE deep-dive, benchmark matrix, share infra details.

Topics: partner program fit; dedicated vs hosted routing; private deployment options; benchmarks and SKUs; security and compliance; go-to-market co-sell motions.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, account lead. Samir from our infra/SE team is with me. How are you all?
[00:12] Priya: Hi Maya, yep I'm Priya, head of partnerships at Veridian. Good to meet you both. We have Jordan and Alex on too.
[00:18] Jordan: Hi all. Quick note we're in SFO but most of our infra people are remote today.
[00:25] Samir: Awesome. We'll keep this high level first then dig into infra details. Goal is to understand Veridian's offering and see where Redwood can integrate (marketplace, dedicated pools, private plane).
[00:35] Priya: The short version: Veridian runs rack-level GPU infrastructure in APAC and EU regions. We sell reserved capacity and bursting, and we just launched a managed inference offering. We're exploring partnerships to give customers more model choices and faster on-ramps.
[00:50] Maya: Nice. Do you typically partner with inference platforms or more with model vendors?
[00:55] Priya: Both. We've done model vendor partnerships but not many inference platform integrations. We see Redwood as interesting because of your dedicated and private deployment modes.
[01:12] Jordan: For context, our customers often need strict residency and low egress. They like predictable latencies. Many of them run LLM workloads but don't want to manage kernels and quantized runtimes themselves.
[01:30] Samir: That resonates. Redwood has three main modes: hosted API, Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools with SLA), and Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). For partners like Veridian we'd look at listing on your marketplace or deploying our private control plane in your customer VPCs. Which of those do you think maps to your GTM?
[01:52] Alex: Marketplace listings are attractive for smaller customers, but our enterprise customers prefer dedicated capacity and control plane isolation. They want KMS integration and audit logs.
[02:05] Maya: Understood. On the security side we provide SOC2 artifacts, KMS/HSM integrations, RBAC, and audit logging. We also have an enterprise checklist for private deployments - happy to share.
[02:15] Priya: Yes please, that checklist will be important. Also, how heavy is the integration work to run Redwood Private in a partner's cloud? Are you doing terraform modules, helm charts, or an OVA?
[02:30] Samir: Good question. For Private we have a deployment package: a customer-managed control plane (kubernetes operator + terraform modules) and a lightweight runtime that we can support via images. For market partnerships we also expose vendor-friendly APIs and a partner SDK. Integration effort depends on network/topology - typically 2-6 weeks with SE support for an initial pilot.
[02:52] Jordan: 2-6 weeks sounds reasonable. For some customers we will need air-gapped options; do you support on-prem packages?
[03:04] Samir: Yes, we have an on-prem option which we've done for regulated customers. There are a few caveats (no external telemetry by default, manual patch windows) but we've run pilots with financial and healthcare customers.
[03:20] Priya: Great. On the pricing side do you prefer revenue share on marketplace or per-seat/commit for Dedicated?
[03:30] Maya: We have flexible models: usage-based hosted pricing, reserved capacity contracts for Dedicated, and enterprise licensing for Private. For marketplace partners we can do revenue share or referral fees. We can send the standard pricing sheet and draft partner terms.
[03:45] Priya: Please send the pricing. Our commercial team will need that to evaluate margin.
[03:52] Samir: We'll include a sample SLA and latency targets we aim for in Dedicated - that's helpful for your sales team.
[04:05] Jordan: On the technical side we wanted to discuss network egress and latency. Many of our customers are in Tokyo and Frankfurt. We need to understand token-per-second performance for 7B and 70B models and the KV cache behavior when doing serving across racks.
[04:25] Samir: We can share perf profiles. Our runtime supports quantized models and KV cache across sessions. For 7B models baseline latency (p50) for short prompts is often under 50ms token time on A100/RTX8000 equivalents with batching disabled; for 70B those increase and require sharding. We'll propose a benchmark matrix to run in your environment.
[04:52] Alex: Can you share the specific SKUs you benchmark on? We have mixtures of NVIDIA H100, A100 and some custom x86+FPGA racks.
[05:03] Samir: We'll include sample SKUs and the kernel configuration we used. Note: H100 generally gives best throughput but also needs optimized kernels; we have profiles for H100/A100/4090-class setups.
[05:20] Priya: One concern from our ops team is multi-tenancy risk. When Redwood runs on a partner host, how do you isolate customer workloads and ensure noisy neighbor problems are mitigated?
[05:34] Samir: We provide pool-level isolation and quota enforcement, physical GPU pinning if needed, and tenant-aware scheduling. For Dedicated customers we can reserve full GPUs or whole nodes. We also provide request-level routing so sensitive workloads can be pinned to isolated pools.
[05:52] Jordan: What about monitoring/metrics? We need per-tenant billing metrics and traces for SLOs.
[06:00] Maya: Our Console includes token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, tracing hooks, and exportable metrics. For partner deployments we can wire the metrics into your pager/observability or export Prometheus metrics.
[06:18] Priya: Perfect. Can you support SAML/SSO and integrate with our identity provider for cross-tenant access?
[06:26] Samir: Yes, SAML and OIDC supported, and RBAC is configurable. We'll document the onboarding steps.
[06:35] Priya: Another question: are there technical blockers around model licensing? Some models customers want are gated or need special license. Can your runtime enforce model-level controls?
[06:47] Samir: We respect model licensing. The runtime can be configured to restrict which model artifacts are available in a deployment and we maintain model catalogs per-tenant. For gated models we'd coordinate licensing with the vendor.
[07:03] Maya: Quick commercial question: partner-led deals, do you want joint selling or just marketplace listing and referral?
[07:12] Priya: Both, ideally. For smaller accounts marketplace/referral is fine, but for enterprise we want co-sell with joint account planning.
[07:20] Maya: Sounds good, we can do both. We'll propose a co-sell playbook in the follow-ups.
[07:28] Jordan: On benchmarks - can Redwood run a small two-hour benchmark on our infra with a sample 7B and 13B model? We'll provide a staging cluster.
[07:38] Samir: Yes, we do partner-run benchmarks. Typically we run a short smoke test then a more representative run. We'll need SSH/K8s access, and a sample dataset. We'll put together a checklist.
[07:52] Alex: Networking: some customers restrict outbound egress to whitelisted endpoints only. Do you have a list of endpoints the Redwood control plane needs to reach?
[08:03] Samir: We'll provide an IP/FQDN allowlist and a minimal set of control plane endpoints. For fully air-gapped we can operate without external calls but there are trade-offs around telemetry and automatic updates.
[08:18] Priya: Good. Any known issues with certain kernel versions or CUDA versions? We run mixed CUDA 11/12 stacks.
[08:28] Samir: We support a range; we'll share compatibility matrix. Some older kernels require backporting. For H100 we recommend CUDA 12+ with patched drivers; we'll include guidance.
[08:42] Maya: Switching gears to GTM, what co-marketing activities interest you? Webinars, joint case studies, marketplace promos?
[08:51] Priya: All of those. Webinars with joint engineering demos are effective. Also we'd like a joint solution brief targeted at financial services.
[08:58] Maya: We'll include a draft brief and a webinar proposal.
[09:05] Jordan: Quick - latency SLOs. Can Redwood route requests by policy (latency vs cost) and fallback to smaller models if capacity constrained?
[09:16] Samir: Yes, smart routing is core to our product. You can set routing policies by customer/route that prefer lower-latency endpoints, fallback models, or cheaper model variants automatically. We'll show this in the SE deep-dive.
[09:31] Priya: One last thing: what level of billing granularity do you expose to partners? We need per-tenant, per-model, per-route cost breakdown for revenue share reconciliation.
[09:43] Maya: Our Console shows token-level cost, per-model cost estimates, and per-API-key usage breakdowns. We can export CSVs or provide an API for billing data.
[09:55] Alex: Okay that will help our billing integration work.
[10:00] Maya: Great - to recap next steps: we'll send deck/pricing, Samir will own the benchmark plan, Veridian will share workload and infra details, and we'll set up an SE deep-dive for next week. Anything else?
[10:12] Priya: That's it from me. Thanks a lot.
[10:18] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll look out for the materials.
[10:22] Samir: Thanks all. We'll follow up with a scheduling poll and the initial checklist.
